title: Cognitive Offloading
finding: Offloading changes the cognitive demands of a task by using external actions or resources. Its consequences depend on the task and on decisions about when to offload.
limit: A conceptual and empirical review, not evidence that generative AI causes lasting cognitive decline.
locator: UCL repository abstract; author manuscript search record.

title: Google Effects on Memory: Cognitive Consequences of Having Information at Our Fingertips
finding: In computer-based memory experiments, expecting later access changed recall of information and its location.
limit: An influential precursor about memory allocation; not an experiment on present-day AI or general intelligence.
locator: Original abstract and authors’ university account; PubMed full-page retrieval encountered CAPTCHA.

title: The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking: Self-Reported Reductions in Cognitive Effort and Confidence Effects From a Survey of Knowledge Workers
finding: 319 workers supplied 936 use examples. Greater confidence in AI was associated with less reported critical thinking.
limit: Self-report and association do not establish loss of cognitive ability over time.
locator: Abstract; sections 4–5 of the primary paper.

title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
finding: In a Turkish high school, unrestricted GPT help improved practice performance but reduced subsequent unaided exam grades by 17% relative to control. A guided tutor largely removed that penalty.
limit: This identifies an effect in a particular learning setting; it does not establish faculty deskilling or permanent cognitive loss.
locator: Published PNAS article supplied by the presenter, abstract p. 1. The August 2025 correction concerns an affiliation, not results: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12403119/

title: Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt when Using an AI Assistant for Essay Writing Task
finding: Essay-writing study with EEG: 54 participants in the first three sessions and 18 in the fourth; reports differences in connectivity and recall across tool conditions.
limit: EEG differences are not a direct measure of permanent cognitive damage. Small task-specific study; retain its preprint status.
locator: arXiv abstract and version history. Included because it is prominent in public discussion, not as the strongest causal evidence.

title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
finding: Specialized agents generate, critique and refine hypotheses. Selected biomedical hypotheses received laboratory evaluation, including drug-repurposing candidates tested in vitro.
limit: Scientists selected and tested hypotheses. These demonstrations do not establish autonomous science across disciplines.
locator: Abstract; Fig. 1; expert-in-the-loop workflow; real-world validations; code-availability statement.

title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
finding: Two shadow evaluations gave agents unpublished AI research questions, six days and substantial compute. Engineering was completed; the original authors judged both papers below the publication bar.
limit: Only two questions; reviews were not blinded. Engineering capability and research judgment are distinct outcomes.
locator: Primary HTML abstract, sections 3–7 and original-author reviews: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27191v1

title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
finding: Time horizon uses human task duration and a specified probability of agent success on the evaluated task suite.
limit: A 50% horizon is neither uninterrupted agent runtime nor a guarantee of successful week-long research.
locator: Methodological details and limitations note. No current leaderboard number is reproduced.

title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
finding: Persistent progress records and incremental work help carry tasks across limited context windows.
limit: An engineering report on software tasks, not a controlled demonstration of scientific discovery. Also shows agents predate 2026.
locator: Long-running agent problem and implementation sections.

title: Harness design for long-running application development
finding: A planner, generator and evaluator divide application-building work, with structured artifacts supporting handoffs.
limit: A vendor engineering case study. More agents and more time do not by themselves validate an output.
locator: Architecture and harness-iteration sections. The presentation diagram is a generic teaching schematic.
